Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalBronze| [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|2009 Mendoza]] | Under-16}} }} '''Anthony Harris Bennett''' (born March 14, 1993) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Al-Najma SC (Bahrain)|Al-Najma]] of the [[Bahraini Premier League (basketball)|Bahraini Premier League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]] (UNLV) for one year. He was the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], becoming the first Canadian to be drafted number one overall.{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Greenberg|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/06/27/anthony-bennett-pick-cavaliers-cleveland_n_3513282.html|title=Anthony Bennett Goes No. 1 In 2013 NBA Draft To Cleveland Cavaliers|work=HuffingtonPost.com|date=June 27, 2013|access-date=June 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414193504/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/anthony-bennett-pick-cavaliers-cleveland_n_3513282 |archive-date=14 April 2023}} He played only four seasons in the NBA, averaging 4.4 points per game, and has been named the worst number-one pick in league history. *{{Cite web |last=Fromal |first=Adam |date=October 4, 2017 |title=The NBA's Worst 1-and-Done Draft Picks of All Time |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2736522-the-nbas-worst-1-and-done-draft-picks-of-all-time |access-date=December 25, 2023 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}} *{{Cite web |last=Irving |first=Kyle |date=2024-06-26 |title=The worst No. 1 picks in NBA Draft history, ranked: Anthony Bennett, Kwame Brown among biggest busts |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/worst-no-1-picks-nba-draft-history-ranked-anthony-bennett-kwame-brown/76a4426d977d25b0aa6101a3 |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[The Sporting News]]}} *{{Cite web |last=Locicero |first=Anthony |date=May 29, 2023 |title=Deadspin {{!}} Anthony Bennett and the NBA Lottery's biggest draft busts of the last decade |url=https://deadspin.com/nba-lottery-draft-bust-anthony-bennett-cavs-knicks-suns-1850480592/ |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[Deadspin]]}} *{{Cite web |date=February 29, 2016 |title=Is Anthony Bennett the worst No. 1 overall pick in NBA history? |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/is-anthony-bennett-the-worst-no-1-overall-pick-in-nba-history |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=[[FOX Sports]]}} *{{Cite web |last=Malhotra |first=Ritvik |date=May 20, 2023 |title=5 worst No. 1 NBA Draft picks of all time |url=https://firstsportz.com/nba-5-worst-no-1-nba-draft-picks-of-all-time/ |access-date=December 25, 2023 |website=FirstSportz}} *{{Cite web |last=Crawford |first=Brad |date=2025-06-23 |title=NBA Draft disasters: Ranking 10 biggest first-round busts in league history |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/nba-draft-disasters-ranking-10-biggest-first-round-busts-in-league-history/ |access-date=2025-11-25 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} ==Early life== Bennett was born on March 14, 1993, in [[Toronto]], Ontario. He was raised in the city's [[Jane and Finch]] neighbourhood, and in nearby [[Brampton]], to where he moved at age ten.{{cite news|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2013/06/28/anthony_bennett_canadian_stars_character_helped_get_him_drafted_no_1.html |title=Anthony Bennett: Canadian star's character helped get him drafted No. 1 |work=TheStar.com |date=June 28, 2013 |access-date=June 28, 2013|last=Smith|first=Doug}}{{cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/canadian-anthony-bennett-welcomed-by-cavaliers-1.1315302 |title=Canadian Anthony Bennett welcomed by Cavaliers |work=CBC.ca |date=June 28, 2013 |access-date=June 28, 2013}} He is the son of Edith Bennett, a [[nursing|nurse]] who is originally from [[Jamaica]], and Delroy Harris. He also has an older sister, Danielle, and an older brother, Sheldon. Edith raised her family as a single mother, working two jobs, at a hospital and a mental health facility.{{cite news |url=http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/anthony_bennett_817643.html |title=Anthony Bennett Bio |work=unlvrebels.com |access-date=June 28, 2013 |archive-date=January 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180124071334/http://www.unlvrebels.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/anthony_bennett_817643.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/7742359/anthony-bennett-mcdonald-all-american-pf-owes-lot-mother |title=Anthony Bennett owes a lot to mom |work=ESPN.com |date=March 27, 2012 |access-date=June 28, 2013|last=Sherman|first=Mitch}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/6/28/4461792/nba-draft-2013-anthony-bennett-canda-cleveland-cavaliers |title=NBA Draft 2013: Anthony Bennett leads the Canadian invasion |work=SBNation.com |date=June 28, 2013 |access-date=June 28, 2013}} As a teenager in Jamaica, his mother ran [[track and field]] and played [[netball]]. Bennett attended [[Harold M. Brathwaite Secondary School]] in Brampton. At age 16, he relocated to [[Beckley, West Virginia|Beckley]], West Virginia, to play basketball for [[Mountain State University#College preparatory school|Mountain State Academy]]. After the school closed a year later, Bennett moved to [[Henderson, Nevada|Henderson]], Nevada, to play for the basketball preparatory academy [[Findlay Prep]]. He was the #1 forward and the #7 player overall in the high school class of 2012 according to [[ESPNU]] 100,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/rankings/_/class/2012 |title=2012 ESPN Basketball Rankings |work=ESPN.com |access-date=June 28, 2013}} the #7 player by [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2012 |title=SCOUT.COM COLLEGE BASKETBALL TEAM RECRUITING PROSPECTS |work=Scout.com |access-date=June 28, 2013}} and the #7 player by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2509 |title=Ranking Index |work=Yahoo.com|access-date=June 28, 2013}} While initially receiving interest from many teams, Bennett narrowed down his college choices to [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. He committed to UNLV under head coach [[Dave Rice (basketball)|Dave Rice]] on May 12, 2012. ==College career== During the [[2012–13 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|2012–13 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball season]], Bennett played 35 games. While mostly starting at [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]], he would occasionally play [[small forward]]. He averaged 16.1 points and 8.1 rebounds a game despite only averaging 27.1 minutes a game due to injury. He shot 53.3% from the field overall and 37.5% from three-point range. He was extremely efficient in college, averaging a PER of 28.3.{{cite web | title=Anthony Bennett Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com| url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/anthony-bennett-1.html |access-date=June 30, 2013}} Halfway through the season, Bennett was plagued with a shoulder injury.{{cite web |last=Pollakoff |first=Brett |date=May 13, 2014 |title=Cavaliers' Anthony Bennett has surgery to improve sleep condition |url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2014/05/13/cavaliers-anthony-bennett-has-surgery-to-improve-sleep-condition/ |access-date=September 23, 2015 |work=NBCSports.com}}{{better source needed|date=March 2017}} His minutes were cut to allow him to rest and he even came off the bench in a few games. UNLV received an at-large berth to the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and lost in the Round of 64 to [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]]. In April 2013, Bennett declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|title=UNLV's Anthony Bennett Officially Declares for the 2013 NBA Draft|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1589592-unlvs-anthony-bennett-offcially-declares-for-the-2013-nba-draft|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131116173842/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1589592-unlvs-anthony-bennett-offcially-declares-for-the-2013-nba-draft|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 16, 2013|work=BleacherReport.com|date=April 2, 2013|access-date=September 23, 2015}} In May 2013, he underwent [[elective surgery]] for [[sleep apnea]] and [[asthma]]. ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2013–2014)=== Bennett was one of thirteen players invited to the green room for the [[2013 NBA draft]], meaning he was expected to be chosen as a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery pick]]. In what CBC described as "a stunning turn of events that surprised even" Bennett, he was selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the Cleveland Cavaliers, making him the first Canadian ever to be selected first overall in an NBA draft.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/cleveland-cavaliers-anthony-bennett-no-1-overall-pick-000748649.html|title=Cleveland Cavaliers take Anthony Bennett with No. 1 overall pick in 2013 NBA draft|date=June 28, 2013|work=Yahoo.com|access-date=June 28, 2013}} He told the media that "I didn't really have any idea who's going No. 1 or who was going No. 2. I heard everything was up for grabs. But I'm just really happy, glad that I have this opportunity, and I've just got to thank God for everything."{{cite news |title=Canadian Anthony Bennett makes NBA history as 1st overall pick {{!}} CBC Sports |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/canadian-anthony-bennett-makes-nba-history-as-1st-overall-pick-1.1323100 |work=CBC |date=June 27, 2013}} On August 20, 2013, Bennett signed a 2-year, $10.9 million rookie scale contract with the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign 2013 Draft Picks to Contracts|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/draft-picks-130820|work=NBA.com|date=August 20, 2013|access-date=September 23, 2015}}{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bennett Contract, Salary Cap Details & Breakdowns |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/houston-rockets/anthony-bennett-13314/transactions/ |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=Spotrac}} After producing multiple mediocre performances to begin his rookie season, he was ranked by some as one of the worst first overall picks in recent memory. He did not score a field goal until his fifth NBA game, and missed his first 16 shot attempts in 43 minutes of playing time.{{cite web|title=Ford: Anthony Bennett Looking Like Worst No. 1 Overall Pick In 20 Years|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/231180/Ford-Anthony-Bennett-Looking-Like-Worst-No-1-Overall-Pick-In-20-Years|work=RealGM.com|date=December 22, 2013|access-date=September 23, 2015}} [[File:Anthony Bennett (10355636284).jpg|thumb|left|200px|Bennett taking a free throw for the Cavaliers in October 2013]] On January 28, 2014, Bennett recorded 15 points and 8 rebounds in a 100–89 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Notebook: Pelicans 100, Cavaliers 89|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140128/NOPCLE/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2014|access-date=September 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301053520/http://www.nba.com/games/20140128/NOPCLE/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 1, 2014|url-status=dead}} It was the first double-figure scoring game in his NBA career, coming after 33 games—three times as long as any previous No. 1 overall pick. Almost two-thirds of all previous top picks scored in double digits in their first game.{{cite news|last=Feldman|first=Dan|title=Anthony Bennett took a really long time to score double-digits|date=January 29, 2014|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/01/29/anthony-bennett-took-a-really-long-time-to-score-double-digits/|access-date=February 5, 2014}} On February 11, 2014, Bennett recorded his first career double-double with 19 points and 10 rebounds in a 109–99 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|title=Notebook: Cavaliers 109, Kings 99|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140211/SACCLE/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 11, 2014|access-date=September 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331233624/http://www.nba.com/games/20140211/SACCLE/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 31, 2014|url-status=dead}} For the 2013–2014 season, he played 52 games while averaging 4.2 points and 3.0 rebounds in 12.8 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Anthony Bennett NBA Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bennean01.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=September 23, 2015}} In July 2014, Bennett joined the Cavaliers for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 13.3 points in four games.{{cite web|title=2014 Summer League Player Profile – Anthony Bennett|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2014/players/sl_anthony_bennett/|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 23, 2015}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2014–2015)=== On August 23, 2014, Bennett was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three-team trade involving the Cavaliers and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/love-three-team-trade|title=Timberwolves Acquire Andrew Wiggins, Anthony Bennett and Thaddeus Young in Three-Team Trade|date=August 23, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=August 23, 2014}} On October 19, 2014, the Timberwolves exercised their third-year team option on Bennett's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]].{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-exercise-team-options-bennett-dieng-and-muhammad |title=Timberwolves Exercise Team Options on Bennett, Dieng and Muhammad |work=NBA.com |date=October 19, 2014 |access-date=October 19, 2014}} On November 21, 2014, he scored a career-high 20 points in a 121–92 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite news |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141121/SASMIN/gameinfo.html |title=Parker's 28 helps Spurs carve up Wolves 121-92 |work=NBA.com |date=November 21, 2014 |access-date=November 21, 2014}} On February 21, 2015, he was ruled out for two weeks due to an injured right ankle he sustained the day before playing against the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=Shabazz Muhammad out for season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12361014/shabazz-muhammad-minnesota-timberwolves-expected-miss-rest-season-finger-surgery|work=ESPN.com|date=February 21, 2015|access-date=September 23, 2015}} After recovering from the injury, Bennett appeared in just four more games to finish the 2014–2015 season. In 57 games (three starts) for the Timberwolves, he averaged career highs of 5.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 15.7 minutes per game.{{Cite web |title=Anthony Bennett Career Stats - NBA in the 2009 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]] and [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]], helping Canada win a bronze medal in each tournament. In the 2010 tournament, he was a teammate of [[Andrew Wiggins]], the number one overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] and his former teammate on the Timberwolves.{{cite web|title=Andrew Wiggins | Canada Basketball|url=http://www.basketball.ca/andrew-wiggins-p149064|access-date=June 27, 2013|work=Basketball.ca|archive-date=January 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104204643/http://www.basketball.ca/andrew-wiggins-p149064|url-status=dead}} In July 2015, Bennett was named to the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]] roster for the [[2015 Pan American Games]].{{cite news|date=July 18, 2015|title=CANADIAN MEN'S BASKETBALL TEAM ANNOUNCED FOR TORONTO 2015 PAN AM GAMES|work=Basketball.ca|url=http://basketball.ca/en/news-article/canadian-mens-basketball-team-announced-for-toronto-2015-pan-am|access-date=July 19, 2015|archive-date=July 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721002240/http://basketball.ca/en/news-article/canadian-mens-basketball-team-announced-for-toronto-2015-pan-am|url-status=dead}} Playing in his hometown of Toronto, Bennett helped Canada win the silver medal with four victories, including an upset win over the United States in the semi-final, before losing in the final to Brazil.
